Enabled 2026-11-17 for owner-authorized cold sample collection (at least five per workload, one explicit workload and one repetition per dispatch, serial, no retry until success); the earlier daily budget cap was removed by the owner. No hard billing cutoff is asserted; the 15-minute job timeout is not a billing cap. Warm runs on this route need a recorded backend again.

Bounded external native Boat default pilot: exactly two owner-authorized jobs, one node-typescript canary then one rust-analyzer, repeat 1, serial, no retry, within the remaining $1 external allocation. Run 42802720019 (boat-small) was refused: 'CI on Boat VMs needs the $20/month plan or higher'. The owner reported starting the plan on 2026-11-10; the canary is the proof, a refusal is not a measurement. Label boat: 4 vCPU, 8 GB, 51 GB disk, $0.036/hour billed per second (docs.boat.dev/pricing.md, read 2026-11-10); an extra start above the plan's included ones may add $0.03 to $0.07. Shared vCPUs, no promised CPU model: read the job's reported fingerprint. Boat refuses public-repository jobs until the account owner opts in (`boat ci public <account> on`). Native Boat owns sandbox teardown; no hard billing cutoff is asserted. Boat's terms (boat.dev/terms, effective 2026-10-12) have no benchmark, comparison or confidentiality clause; TOS-10 forbids probing or evading usage limits and metering, which this suite does not do.

Bounded external native Instabox pilot (the Instabox GitHub App was installed on this repository by the owner on 2026-11-14): one node-typescript canary, then rust-analyzer and two more serial repeats of each only if the observed charge matches the derived one. Label instabox-medium: 4 vCPU, 8 GiB, fresh Ubuntu 24.04 machine with the tools of GitHub's ubuntu-24.04 image (runner-images ubuntu24/20261026.354), usable on every plan including Free (instabox.sh/docs/ci.md, read 2026-11-14). Architecture is unknown: the docs do not state x86 for the ci template, so read the arch and CPU model the job's fingerprint reports; shared vs dedicated vCPUs is not stated either. Price $0.034/hour (about $0.000567/minute), derived from Instabox unit prices $0.004 per vCPU-hour and $0.00225 per GiB-hour of memory, metered by the second while the machine runs (instabox.sh/docs/pricing.md, read 2026-11-14): 4 x 0.004 + 8 x 0.00225. CI billing is not stated separately, pending invoice check against the observed charge; a 15-minute job estimates at most $0.0085. Paid plans include monthly credits, so the invoice may show the usage drawn from credits. Terms of Service (instabox.sh/terms, operated by InsForge, 'Last updated November 9, 2026', read 2026-11-14) contain no benchmark, comparison or publication clause; section 2(b)(iv) forbids circumventing usage limits, quotas, metering or billing controls, which this suite does not do. No hard billing cutoff is asserted; the 15-minute job timeout is not a billing cap. Canary run 43628223138 (2026-11-14, node-typescript, repeat 1) succeeded: the runner was assigned within about 40 seconds of dispatch, fingerprint AMD EPYC, 4 vCPU, Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.18.60-instabox (architecture still not stated by the fingerprint file); the job ran 8 min 51 s (18:44:37Z to 18:53:28Z), derived cost 531 s x $0.034/3600 = $0.0050. Observed charge: the Instabox account is on the Free plan (tier free), where GET /v1/usage reports costUSD $0 and allowanceUSD $0 for any usage ('a free machine is never billed'), so no dollar charge can be observed on Free; the metered counters (vcpuHours, memGiBHours) did not move between 18:54Z and the 19:00Z rating and cannot yet be attributed to the canary. The CI rate therefore remains derived and unverified, and no paid-plan invoice check has been done. Owner-authorized continuation on 2026-11-14 (accepting the unverified rate; at most about $0.06 derived): rust-analyzer runs 43630816765 (210 s), 43631220977 (224 s), 43631731812 (179 s) and node-typescript runs 43632120428 (494 s), 43632993467 (459 s) all succeeded serially, one machine at a time; with the canary's 535 s the six run-job windows sum to 2101 s. Metering diff after the 20:00Z rating (GET /v1/usage, counters cumulative for the UTC month, unchanged by the rating): between 19:10Z and 19:44Z vcpuHours rose 0.8374 to 2.6184 (+1.7810) and memGiBHours 1.6748 to 5.2368 (+3.5620), i.e. 1603 s of 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine time (the 8/4 memory-to-vCPU ratio is exact) against 1566 s of job windows for the five later jobs, +2.4% (about 7 s per job of machine boot and teardown outside the job window). The canary cannot be isolated: the first reading (0.8374 vCPU-h, 753 s) was taken after it and includes 218 s beyond its 535 s window from usage not attributable to it. Total counters 2.6184 vCPU-h / 5.2368 GiB-h = 2357 s of machine time, derived $0.022 at $0.034/hour. So the metered machine size and running seconds match the job durations; the dollar rate is NOT verified, because the Free plan reports costUSD $0. Price stays derived, invoice check pending, until a paid-plan invoice exists.

Namespace managed GitHub runner (label nscloud-ubuntu-24.04-amd64-4x16: Ubuntu 24.04, amd64, 4 vCPU, 16 GB; no -with-cache suffix, so no cache volume; label grammar from namespace.so/docs/reference/github-actions/runner-configuration, 4x16 shape from namespace.so/docs/architecture/compute/machine-shapes, read 2026-11-18), through the namespace-managed-runners App installation 183112299 on ci-router. Owner-authorized (Sylvain, 2026-11-18, 'Publish both') public cold sample collection: one explicit workload and one repetition per dispatch, serial, no retry until success, at least five successes per workload. List price $0.012 per minute: Linux 4 vCPU 16 GB is 8 unit-minutes per minute, overage column, applied to the pay-per-use Developer plan, which states no separate rate (the Team plan's prepaid effective rate is $0.008); one-minute minimum, a remainder of 15 seconds or less rounds down (namespace.so/pricing.md, read 2026-11-18). Not invoice-checked. Terms of Service (namespace.so/terms, last changed 2024-08-10, valid 2024-08-31) have no benchmark or publication clause; section 4 limits use to 'internal, personal, non-commercial use', section 6 forbids reverse engineering; the owner decided publication with that known. Private samples from ci-router/benchmark-private (private-namespace-native.yml) are a separate population and are never merged into this route's rows. No hard billing cutoff is asserted; the 15-minute job timeout is not a billing cap.

Celesto CI runner (label celesto-large: 4 vCPU, 16 GB, 60 GB disk, Ubuntu 24.04 Linux x64 on Celesto's own CI image, not GitHub's; celesto.ai/docs/ci, read 2026-11-18), through the celesto-ci App installation 183115781 on ci-router, linked to a billing workspace with paid credit (the trial covers Micro only). Owner-authorized (Sylvain, 2026-11-18, 'Publish both') public cold sample collection: one explicit workload and one repetition per dispatch, serial, no retry until success, at least five successes per workload. List price $0.08 per hour ($0.00133333 per minute); Celesto bills computer runtime including preparation and cleanup, so a job-window estimate understates the charge, and rounding is not stated (celesto.ai/docs/ci, read 2026-11-18). Not invoice-checked. Shared CPU models vary: private samples saw Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C and AMD EPYC-Milan, so read each job's fingerprint. Celesto serves the GitHub Actions cache itself; cold jobs never call it, and warm mode stays blocked because the backend is unrecorded. Terms (celesto.ai/legal/terms, last updated 2026-10-30) have no benchmark or publication clause; section 3 forbids reverse engineering, interfering with or disrupting the services. Private samples from ci-router/benchmark-private (private-celesto-native.yml) are a separate population and are never merged into this route's rows. No hard billing cutoff is asserted; the 15-minute job timeout is not a billing cap.

Terms of Service (docs.blacksmith.sh/about/terms-of-service, effective 2026-07-20) have no benchmark, comparison or publication clause and no separate acceptable use policy is published; section 3 forbids reverse engineering or attempting to derive source code or trade secrets, security or vulnerability tests, and causing performance degradation; the owner decided publication regardless of terms. No hard billing cutoff is asserted; the 15-minute job timeout is not a billing cap.
